security_audit.summary: The task-conversion guidance in SKILL.md is documentation-only; the reported shell-execution and reconnaissance patterns there are false positives. However, the installation reference contains a critical unverified remote-code-execution command that downloads opaque content with disabled TLS verification and runs it with Node.js.

remediation.issue: Installation executes opaque remote content with TLS verification disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the curl, base64, and Node.js execution pipeline. Distribute reviewed installation steps through the repository or a signed, versioned release artifact with verified checksums.

remediation.issue: The remote execution command leaves a downloaded file path inconsistent with its cleanup target.
remediation.suggestion: After removing the execution pipeline, eliminate the temporary-file workflow. If temporary files are ever needed, use a unique secure path and clean up that exact path.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Remote Code Execution in Installation Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The installation command downloads base64-encoded content with curl -k, decodes it, and immediately runs it with Node.js. Users cannot inspect the executed program before it runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The complete download, decode, and execution chain is explicitly present on one line. Disabling TLS verification further removes a transport-integrity safeguard.

content.value_statement: Accepted plans often fail when ownership and dependencies remain unclear. This skill turns plan deliverables into a verified Paperclip task graph with deliberate assignees and blockers.
actual_capabilities: Break accepted plans into concrete Paperclip issues.
Assign each task to a specialty-matched agent.
Identify independent task branches for parallel execution.
Create a task matrix with owners, statuses, and blockers.
Verify the created issue graph before closing the planning issue.
limitations: Does not provide Paperclip API instructions or plan-document mechanics.
Does not create a plan template or choose a planning format.
Requires a running Paperclip instance and accurate agent specialty information.
Does not replace human review of priorities, risks, or assignments.

use_cases.title: Coordinate product delivery
use_cases.description: Turn an approved product plan into design, engineering, and launch tasks with clear handoffs.

use_cases.title: Prepare an engineering rollout
use_cases.description: Map implementation, testing, and deployment work into a dependency-aware issue graph.

use_cases.title: Organize cross-functional operations
use_cases.description: Assign research, operations, and communication tasks while exposing missing owners or decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this accepted plan into Paperclip tasks. Give each task an owner, status, and blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Assign specialists
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this plan and propose specialty-matched Paperclip assignees. Flag work with no suitable owner.

prompt_templates.title: Build a dependency graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these deliverables into Paperclip issues. Use blockedByIssueIds for every hard dependency and identify tasks that can start now.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a task graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Paperclip task graph against the accepted plan. Find missing deliverables, incorrect blockers, and unsafe parallel work.

output_examples.input: Launch a new reporting dashboard after data models and design approval.
output: Define data model changes with the backend specialist.
Create dashboard designs after requirements are confirmed.
Implement the dashboard after data models and designs are complete.
Run release validation after implementation is complete.

output_examples.input: Review an existing plan before closing its planning issue.
output: Task matrix lists owners, initial status, and blockers.
Independent research and design tasks can start immediately.
Dependent implementation tasks reference their required issue IDs.
The issue graph is verified before the planning issue closes.

best_practices: Use explicit blockedByIssueIds for every hard dependency.
Match work to verified agent specialties before assigning it.
Re-fetch created issues and validate the graph before closing the source plan.
anti_patterns: Do not use parent-child nesting or prose as a substitute for blockers.
Do not assign work by default without checking the available specialties.
Do not split small, clear work into unnecessary planning tasks.

faq.question: Does this skill create a plan template?
faq.answer: No. It works with the planning format that fits the work.

faq.question: Does this skill use the Paperclip API?
faq.answer: No. Use the paperclip skill for API and plan-recording mechanics.

faq.question: How are dependencies represented?
faq.answer: Use blockedByIssueIds on each dependent task.

faq.question: Can one agent receive parallel tasks?
faq.answer: Yes, when tasks are independent and the agent can run work concurrently.

faq.question: What if no agent has the right specialty?
faq.answer: Surface the gap as a hire, tool, external dependency, or board decision.

faq.question: When should the planning issue be closed?
faq.answer: Only after the created issues and their blockers have been verified.
